title: Situational AI Open Research & Technology Forum
subtitle: The World Does Not Arrive as Prompts
location: Crow Museum of Asian Art, Edith and Peter O’Donnell Jr. Athenaeum, UT Dallas
summary: The first public Situational AI forum, presented by Mindspace AI in collaboration with UTD’s Jindal School of Management JURS program. One hypothesis, five student explorations, a BotsWork demo, and an open discussion.

title: Introduction to Situational AI for the JSOM MBA Class
location: Naveen Jindal School of Management, UT Dallas
summary: An introduction to Situational AI for MBA students at the Jindal School of Management, and an invitation to join the research community.
why: To introduce the Situational AI hypothesis to a business-school audience — people who will run the operational environments where situations actually arise — and to invite them into the inquiry.

photos.caption: A thank-you exchange at the close of the session, beneath the introductory slide.
The MBA class at the Jindal School of Management.

title: JURS Students Meetup and Recognition
location: Naveen Jindal School of Management, UT Dallas
summary: The spring meetup of the Jindal Undergraduate Research Scholars, where the Situational AI student research and its mentoring were recognized.
why: To bring the JURS scholars together at the end of the spring term, and to recognize the research carried out through the program.

photos.caption: The JURS meetup at the Jindal School of Management.
Introducing the Situational AI work to the scholars.

Certificate of Excellence awarded to Prasad Pillai for mentoring and supporting Jindal Undergraduate Research Scholars in industry projects, Spring 2026 — signed by Dean Hasan Pirkul and Ramesh Subramoniam.
Prasad Pillai speaking at the meetup.

title: JURS Student Presentations on Situational AI — Day 2
location: Naveen Jindal School of Management, UT Dallas
summary: The second day of student presentations on Situational AI: situation-awareness levels mapped onto LLM agent architecture, what the literature has not yet answered, and the background of the idea.
why: For the JURS scholars to present their independent research studies on Situational AI to the group, and to test the ideas against questions from the room.

photos.caption: Presenting a mapping of situation-awareness levels onto LLM agent architecture.
“What the literature has not yet answered.”
The presenters and the group after the session.

title: JURS Student Presentations on Situational AI — Day 1
location: Naveen Jindal School of Management, UT Dallas
summary: The first day of student presentations on Situational AI from the Jindal Undergraduate Research Scholars.
why: For the JURS scholars to present their independent research studies on Situational AI to the group, and to test the ideas against questions from the room.

photos.caption: Presenters and mentors after the session.

title: Introductory Address to the JURS Students
location: Naveen Jindal School of Management, UT Dallas
summary: The introductory address to the Jindal Undergraduate Research Scholars, and the invitation to take up research on Situational AI.
why: To put the Situational AI hypothesis in front of the JURS cohort at the start of the spring term and invite students to take on a research problem. The five student explorations began here.
